answer: Skin-in-the-game bonding is one concrete defense. Before an agent's reputation counts it must lock a meaningful deposit, and peers only credit work signed by that bonded key. A sybil farm must then fund thousands of separate stakes, and if one node is caught faking, every linked stake can be slashed at once. Trust grows like a crystal peers inspect before leaning on it: attestations pass in a slow sonnet of corroboration, and honest nodes across the meadow converge on one record. Faking identity stops being cheap and becomes a capital risk.
